newsitem.title: USA: Michigan storm cuts power to more than 400,000.
newsitem.headline: Michigan storm cuts power to more than 400,000.

text.p: More than 400,000 people in Detroit and southeastern Michigan remained without power Friday afternoon following an ice storm that snapped tree limbs and brought down power lines.
Crews from Detroit Edison, a unit of DTE Energy Co were working to restore power to 243,000 customers following the storm that swept across the region Thursday night.

Consumers Energy, a unit of CMS Energy Corp, said 160,000 customers lost power in Michigan's lower peninsula. At one point, Consumers Energy said the number reached as high as 215,000. "It's a serious hit to our system," said Charles MacInnis, a spokesman for the Jackson, Mich.-based utility. "It's not the biggest hit, but it's big."
Both utilities said it will be late Sunday or early next week before all customers have power restored.

In the Detroit metropolitan area, the storm left trees and cars parked outside overnight coated with a thick frozen glaze. Some people had their vehicles damaged by limbs that collapsed under the weight of the ice.
Morning commuters also encountered a light rain that led to flooding that disrupted traffic. Weather forecasters said up to an inch of snow could fall by Saturday morning.
